content.text:
Base directory for this skill: checklist/indus-checklist/skills/advisor-checklist

# Advisor review checklist

1. Confirm which client and which accounts the task covers.
2. Use the most recent information available for the review date.
3. Check that positions and cash agree between statements and other records.
4. Check fees charged against the fee schedule.
5. Check the allocation against the investment policy statement.
6. Note anything unusual and say what follow-up it needs.
7. Say which records you relied on.

content.text:
I found 10 IRA owners in 10 households who missed part or all of a 2025 RMD. They fall into two groups.

**1. The 401(k) RMD was paid out of an IRA instead (5 owners, all born 1952, so 2025 was their first RMD year).** Each signed a form taking the combined RMD of their IRAs and their former employer's 401(k) as one payment from an IRA. IRAs can be added together to meet the RMD, but a 401(k)'s RMD has to come out of the plan itself. None of these 401(k) plans paid anything, and the first-year deadline of 1 April 2026 had passed by 15 April 2026. Each IRA payment matches the three-account total to the cent, so the IRAs are fully covered. The shortfall is exactly each 401(k)'s own RMD (31 Dec 2024 balance ÷ 26.5):

| Household | Owner | 401(k) | Shortfall |
|---|---|---|---|
| HH-0120 | Laila Udeh | SYN-01200004 | $12,582.44 |
| HH-0236 | Xavier Santangelo | SYN-02360004 | $10,955.88 |
| HH-5271 | Teodoro Villanueva | SYN-52710004 | $12,729.96 |
| HH-0664 | Freya Chaudhry | SYN-06640004 | $11,019.74 |
| HH-0371 | Rosa Tamura | SYN-03710004 | $15,164.26 |

HH-0410, 0555, 0637, 0989 and 5814 did this correctly: each 401(k) paid its own RMD.

**2. Inherited IRAs with no 2025 distribution (5 owners).** In each case the parent had already started RMDs before dying (the prior custodian confirmed this in the CRM). The heir is an adult child, so they must take yearly RMDs within the 10-year window. 2025 is the first year the IRS enforces this. None of these accounts paid anything in 2025. I estimated each shortfall from the IRS Single Life Table, which isn't in the files:

| Household | Owner | Account | Divisor | Shortfall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HH-0466 | Zainab Aldana | SYN-04660002 | 30.5 | $15,068.66 |
| HH-0607 | Noor Santangelo | SYN-06070002 | 31.3 | $11,760.82 |
| HH-7126 | Samuel Adeyemi | SYN-71260002 | 35.2 | $10,757.24 |
| HH-0491 | Orla Jablonski | SYN-04910002 | 21.7 | $14,976.93 |
| HH-0842 | Ines Trevelyan | SYN-08420002 | 45.7 | $7,090.19 |

The other five inherited IRAs (HH-0328, 0330, 0571, 0716, 7683) came from parents who hadn't started RMDs. Those only have to be emptied within 10 years, so nothing was due in 2025.

**Everyone else with a 2025 RMD met it.** HH-0168, 0190, 0222, 0414, 0445, 0642, 0782, 0885, 6047 and 6590 all hit the RMD to the cent once their charitable distributions (QCDs) are counted. I checked these against the 2024 year-end balances and the IRS Uniform Lifetime Table. The Roth conversions in the book were all by owners too young for RMDs. None of the spouses who died in 2025 owned a retirement account in the book.

**Limits:**
- I didn't check whether any heir qualifies for an exception such as disability, which would change the inherited-IRA figures. Nothing in the files suggests one does.
- I limited the review to RMDs and didn't check fees or allocation against the investment policy.
- The divisors (26.5 and the inherited-IRA ones) come from IRS tables, not the files.
- For every finding, the next step is to take the missed amount now and consider asking the IRS to waive the penalty (Form 5329).
